correctness.rationale: All 10/12-side polygons in the precise equality family are parametrized by a rank-two closed edge-length constraint. The Wigner shoelace area is an exact quadratic form, strictly positive away from symmetry by Brunn–Minkowski and its equality case. A strictly convex quadratic maximizes over the compact cube section at vertices. Every vertex must have n-2 saturated cube coordinates, giving an exhaustive 80/240 two-equation active-set calculation. The embedded exact symbolic checker confirms 12/28 distinct vertices, five signed-cyclic orbits and their exact areas; it reconstructs independent sample polygon shoelace sums. From the orbit maxima and the exact regular-symmetral area, the normalized sharp constants and strict nonmonotone inequality follow algebraically. The boundary-only maximizing vectors and scaling give nonattainment and sharp approach. Finite enumeration is exhaustive only because the active-set theorem reduces the continuum maximum to those cases.

value.rationale: The 2026 improved-isoperimetry equality family is infinite-dimensional across side counts, and its internal Wigner asymmetry is not resolved by the universal bound. The complete sharp 10/12-sided classification displays unexpected nonmonotone behavior: all 12 vertices of the 10-side parameter polytope maximize, versus just 4 of 28 for 12 sides. These exact constants and the commensurability-driven vertex-orbit split provide concrete finite polygonal benchmarks for studying discrete-to-smooth constant-width behavior. The result is a joint structural classification and a qualitative boundary phenomenon, not a routine substitution or isolated table lookup.
